Samantha / Evelyn — quick read of the attached template. High-level: nothing unusual, but three items to flag for negotiation/clarity before we redline formally: 

1) Subprocessor notification vs approval — the template currently requires prior written approval for new subprocessors. Our standard is notice + objection window (we can accept a 10-business-day review period). If DataForge needs approval rights, we'll need to understand the specific categories they want reserved.

2) Data retention and deletion timing — clause states "30 days" for deletion after contract termination; Redwood's default is 60 days. We can accommodate shorter if they have a legal requirement, but prefer 60 in the standard.

3) Transfer mechanism language — SCCs are fine, but we prefer embedding our standard SCC addendum rather than modifying clause language directly. If DataForge requires additional safeguards (e.g., encryption-at-rest proof or audits), we can provide evidence but might require an expo timeline.

If DataForge shares a mark-up, we can produce a tracked redline by EOD Friday. Evelyn/Laura — please collect the subprocessor export and let me know if any vendor in their CSV is a restricted provider (e.g., analytics vendors that persist raw data).

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

On an operational note: Redwood's DocuSign envelope templates already include a DPA execution flow; let us know if they prefer AdobeSign and we'll route accordingly.

Thanks for the quick turn. A few replies inline: 

- Approval vs notification: we usually ask for approval for subprocessors that handle sensitive PII or payment data. I'll pull a short list of categories (PII, financial, security-logging) — we are happy to work with a 10-business-day objection window for other categories.
- Deletion window: our compliance team prefers 30 days, but that's not a hard blocker if you document the retention and deletion process.
- SCCs: fine to use your SCC addendum; we will still request encryption-at-rest confirmation and the date of your last SOC 2 (Type II) report.

We'd like a simple mapping CSV (1:1) so our procurement can compare. Also prefer DocuSign; please send a standard envelope link once you have a redline.

Samantha
